place: A town in regional Victoria, Australia
about: Every place-specific figure the town generator uses, with its source. A world for another place and time is another profile; the platform's code holds none of these (docs/profiles.md).

unions.teaching: Together, workers win better pay and conditions than each alone.

kinds.name: congregation
kinds.teaching: There is a God who made the world and cares how we live.

sources.currency: Australian dollars, in cents: written with a dollar sign before the amount ("$1,234.56"), or in words as dollars (informally bucks) and cents. ISO 4217: AUD, two decimal places.
sources.health: The clinic stands for the town's health system (general practice and the hospital it refers to; a liberty: a town of 200 has neither). doctors_per_1000: about 120 full-time-equivalent GPs per 100,000 people (Department of Health and Aged Care, GP workforce statistics, 2023; to confirm). doctor_wage_per_pay_period: a salaried GP in community health, about $180,000 a year (placeholder, to source from the Victorian public sector's agreements). consult_minutes: a long consultation (MBS item 36 is 20-40 minutes; placeholder for care of a hospital-level condition). seek_care_bps, treats and off_work_severities: placeholders (the conditions here are hospital-level, so nearly everyone with one is treated; care shortens them by a fifth; fatal_kept_bps has no effect while conditions don't kill: docs/behaviour/life.md). Nobody works with a serious or severe condition (a hospital stay): placeholder.
sources.round: Working hours 9 to 5, Monday to Friday, for everyone, shops included (a liberty: shops open Saturdays with rostered staff, not modelled); school 9 to 3 on school days (Victorian school hours are about 8:50 to 3:20). Travel: off the roads, a 25 m cell on foot in about 18 seconds (walking about 1.4 m/s: Bohannon 1997; to confirm); on a road, about 2 seconds (45 km/h, under the default urban limit of 50 km/h, Road Safety Road Rules 2017 (Vic); to confirm; most regional Victorians drive to work: ABS Census 2021, method of travel to work); slower across water, wetland and bush (placeholders). Roads: the town builds toward buildings more than three cells (75 m) from one (placeholder), within a roads budget of about $300 a resident a year (Victorian councils' spending on local roads, Victorian Local Government Grants Commission; placeholder, to confirm).
sources.ownership: house_owner_bps: about 72% of separate houses in Victoria are owner-occupied (ABS, Census 2021, tenure by dwelling structure; to confirm); flats here are all rented (a liberty: strata titles aren't modelled). mortgage_bps_by_age: of owner-occupiers, the share still repaying a mortgage by the household head's age (placeholder shaped by ABS, Housing Occupancy and Costs: most under 45 have one, few over 65; to confirm). mortgage_payment_per_month: the median monthly mortgage repayment in Victoria, $1,733 (ABS, Census 2021; to confirm). mortgage_rate_bps: an owner-occupier variable rate, about 6.2% (RBA lending rates, 2025; to confirm). mortgage_years_left: placeholder. market (buying and selling homes): a 20% deposit, as lenders ask to lend without mortgage insurance (APRA's prudential guidance on LVRs; to confirm); costs about 5% of the price, mostly stamp duty (State Revenue Office Victoria's land transfer duty rates; to confirm); a 30-year term, the usual for a new home loan (to confirm); buy_bps_per_month: the chance a renting household that could afford a home that suits it buys in a month, a placeholder (to calibrate against ABS lending indicators, first home buyers); relist_days and cut_bps: a home unsold after a month is listed again 5% cheaper, down to 80% of the first asking price (placeholders: sellers commonly cut their asking price the longer a home is on the market, Merlo and Ortalo-Magné 2004; to confirm).
sources.utilities: Water: residential use about 160 litres a person a day in regional Victoria (Essential Services Commission, water performance reports; to confirm); a regional water corporation's tariff, about $3 a kilolitre and $90 a quarter in service charges (to confirm against a corporation's price determination); bills go to owners. The river's inflow, flow and losses are placeholders, sized so a small town's draw is a small share of a modest river's water. Energy (electricity): an average Victorian household uses about 4,000 kWh a year, 11 a day (Australian Energy Regulator / ESC; to confirm); the Victorian Default Offer for 2025-26 is about 30 cents a kWh and $1.10 a day in supply charges (ESC; to confirm); what the retailer pays the grid (wholesale and network), placeholder; grid emissions about 0.78 kg CO2e a kWh (National Greenhouse Accounts Factors 2024, Victoria, scope 2; to confirm).
sources.climate: Weather drawn for each run (docs/behaviour/weather.md). rain_by_month_bps: river flows in inland Victoria are highest in winter and spring and lowest in late summer (Bureau of Meteorology, climate statistics and water data; shape a placeholder, to confirm). storm_*: a heavy-rain spell in about one month in twelve, two to four days at two and a half times the usual inflow (placeholder, to calibrate against flood frequency: Victorian Floodplain Management Strategy). drought_*: about one year in twelve begins a drought of six to eighteen months at 40% of usual inflow (placeholder; the Millennium Drought ran far longer). Heatwaves: three to five days, about one summer week in eight (two or so a summer: Bureau of Meteorology heatwave service; placeholder); built ground hotter than open land (the urban heat island); each unit of heat adds 1% a year to the chance of illness, so a heatwave about doubles an adult's illness for its days (the January 2009 Victorian heatwave: ambulance call-outs up 46%, deaths up 62% over the week, Department of Human Services 2009; to confirm). warning_lead_days: the Bureau warns a couple of days ahead (placeholder).
sources.hazards: Floods (world-expansion 7.3), placeholders sized against the river as modelled (about 9,000 kL a 25 m cell in the usual flow): it spills over its banks past 12,000, 30% of the excess a day; a building floods with water above 300 kL on its cell (about half a metre over 625 m2); wetland soaks up 500 kL a cell a day, so draining it floods more downstream (the floodplain function of wetlands: to source, e.g. Victorian floodplain management guidance). Councils run emergency relief centres (Emergency Management Act 2013 (Vic); to confirm): here the town hall.
sources.crime: Crime (world-expansion 7.2), deliberately rare and driven by circumstance only (need and opportunity, and the chance of being caught: Becker 1968; Cohen and Felson 1979), never by any group. take_bps_per_month_in_need, caught_bps_reckoned and take_quantity: placeholders. detection_bps: about one theft in five is solved (Crime Statistics Agency Victoria, offences resolved; to confirm). police_per_1000: about 2.3 sworn officers per 1,000 Victorians (Victoria Police annual report; to confirm). officer_wage_per_pay_period: a senior constable, about $100,000 a year (Victoria Police enterprise agreement; to confirm). investigation_hours: placeholder.
sources.justice: The tribunal is a civil and administrative tribunal of the state (VCAT is the model: residential tenancies and civil claims lists). hearing_after_days: about three weeks from application to hearing (placeholder; VCAT's annual report gives times to finalise by list, to source). pay_within_days: placeholder. challenge_bps: the share of tenants given an unlawful notice of rent increase who apply to the tribunal, and apply_bps: the share of workers owed wages who pursue a claim (placeholders: few do; to source, e.g. from Consumer Affairs Victoria and Fair Work Ombudsman reports). apply_after_days: a month's wait for payment first (placeholder). Enforcement of an unpaid money order by an order to the debtor's bank (a garnishee order, Judgment Debt Recovery Act 1984 (Vic), to confirm).
sources.education: school_ages: Victorian children start school (Prep) in the year they turn 5 and must attend until 17 (Education and Training Reform Act 2006 (Vic); to confirm the section). students_per_teacher: about 13.5 full-time-equivalent students per teacher in Victoria (ABS, Schools, 2024; to confirm). school_days_per_year: about 200 (four terms of about ten weeks). hours_per_day: about 6 (placeholder). teacher_wage_per_pay_period: about $110,000 a year, near the top of the classroom teacher range in the Victorian Government Schools Agreement 2022 (to confirm). attainment: the highest level of education of Australians aged 25-64 (ABS, Education and Work, May 2024; shares rounded, to confirm), as years of schooling (Year 11 or below as 10: placeholder). return_per_year_bps: the wage return to a year of schooling, about 10% (Leigh 2008, 'Returns to education in Australia', Economic Papers 27(3); estimates run 8-15%; to confirm), taken as productivity (human capital: Mincer 1974) and applied linearly in the time a task takes (docs/behaviour/education.md). max_years: the skill scale's top (placeholder).
sources.elections: Local Government Act 2020 (Vic): councils are elected every four years (general elections, the last in October 2024), voting is compulsory for those enrolled, and single-councillor wards vote by preference. This town elects its mayor directly (most Victorian mayors are chosen by the councillors: a liberty). Turnout, about 83% (the VEC's reported participation at the 2024 local elections, to confirm). stand_bps (the chance an adult stands when an election is called, before their drive: 2%, a placeholder to calibrate against candidates per vacancy, the VEC's) and news_readers_bps (the share who read the local paper each week) are placeholders: the University of Canberra's Digital News Report: Australia gives local news use, to source.
sources.nature: Nature (docs/design/world-expansion.md 2). cell_m: a cell is a 25 m lot (a town of 1,000 at about 13 people a hectare). The landscape around the town (margin_cells, block_cells, shares_bps, woodland_patches), the covers' succession (cleared land to grassland in a year; scrub to woodland in about 40), the pollution figures, survey_hours_per_ha and survey_staff (the town's environment office: one scientist) are placeholders. spin_up_years: nature is run alone this long before the start, so it begins in its own balance (as ecological and climate models spin up).
sources.nature.species: Placeholders for growth, mortality, dispersal, min_viable and detection. Gliders and fairy-wrens live in family groups sharing a home range, which isn't modelled, so their breeding threshold is one; frogs breed where at least four share a pond (a home range of half a hectare). How far each crosses ground it can’t live on (dispersal_m): frogs up to 200 m from water (the frog’s guidelines above); gliders glide gaps of tens of metres (75 m, a placeholder); fairy-wrens, placeholder. The young always leave their parents' home range (natal dispersal, in the physics); the share of adults moving a year is a placeholder. Densities and ranges: squirrel glider (listed under Victoria's Flora and Fauna Guarantee Act 1988), 0.38 a hectare in Victoria and a home range of 3-5 ha (van der Ree and others, from the studies summarised in 'Large area used by squirrel gliders in an urban area', PMC8216951; to confirm against the originals), crossing cleared gaps badly; growling grass frog (listed; nationally vulnerable), about 68 adults at a Melbourne wetland (45 males and 23 females, Heard and others; to confirm), moving 15-200 m between waterbodies and living as a metapopulation, sensitive to water quality ('Guidelines for managing the endangered Growling Grass Frog in urbanising landscapes'; the EPBC species profile); superb fairy-wren, a common and conspicuous control, territories of 1-2 ha held by a pair and helpers (Museums Victoria), densities by cover a placeholder.
sources.households: ABS, Census of Population and Housing 2021 (QuickStats, Australia): lone person 25.6%, group 3.9%, family 70.5% of households; of families, couple without children 38.8%, with children 43.7%, one parent 15.9%, other 1.6% (counted with groups). Children per family: AIFS, from the 2021 Census (3+ taken as 3). Same-sex couples 1.4% (Census 2021); one in five lone parents male (Census 2021); 105.8 boys per 100 girls (ABS, Births, Australia 2024). Placeholders: adult_female_bps (about half), group_size, mother_age_at_first_birth (around the median age of mothers, 32.1, ABS Births 2024), adult_ages (18 to 99: the bounds; adults' ages are drawn from the census bands, households.age_bands_bps).
sources.life.qx_per_100000: ABS, Life Tables 2021-2023 (Table 9, Australia): the probability of dying within a year, ages 0-100, per 100,000, males and females.
sources.life.illness: Placeholder shaped by AIHW's age gradient of hospitalisations (99 per 1,000 at 5-14, 1,511 at 85+; 153 overnight per 1,000 overall, 2022-23); to replace with age-specific overnight rates.
sources.life.injury: AIHW: 2,100 injury hospitalisations per 100,000 people (2022-23). Severity split: placeholder.
sources.life.birth: Bearing a child from 15 to 49 (ABS age-specific fertility rates cover 15-49); 38 weeks from conception; 105.8 boys per 100 girls (ABS Births 2024).
sources.life.treatable: The share of deaths that timely, effective health care could have prevented (treatable mortality, as the OECD and Eurostat define it: under 75 only). About 15% of deaths under 75 in Australia (AIHW, Deaths in Australia: potentially avoidable deaths, about half of deaths under 75, a third of them treatable; to confirm against the tables). Carried by the severe illness band, whose fatality by age the generator sets so that, with care as usual (the profile's seek_care_bps, and care cutting a death to health.treats' fatal_kept_bps), each age dies at the life table's rate; without care, more die.
sources.life.found_alone_after: How long after dying at home alone a person is found. No figure for Victoria or Australia was found, so Japan's is used, the one country found to count it: National Police Agency of Japan, people who died alone at home in 2025 (76,941): found the same or the next day 28,398; in 2 to 3 days 15,865; in 4 to 7 days 10,456; in 8 days or more 22,222, of them 7,148 after a month or more and 208 after a year or more. Read 2026-10-08 as reported in the press (a summary of the agency's release), not in the agency's own tables (to confirm). The last band is closed at a year (208 of 76,941 were longer). Japan's share of people living alone and its neighbourhood ties are its own: a placeholder for a local figure.
sources.life.work_injury_bps: Safe Work Australia, Key WHS Statistics 2024 (2023-24): serious claims (a week or more off), at about 1,700 hours a year: manufacturing 9.4 per million hours; all industries 6.8 (a placeholder for retail).
sources.pay_period_days: Added 2026-10-08 by the platform change that made this a profile figure; needs its author's check. 14 days, because this profile's wages are stated for fourteen days (where pay here is monthly, its author converted them: see wages_per_pay_period). To set to the place's own pay period, with the wages restated for it.
sources.wages_per_pay_period: Shop: the award minimum, General Retail Industry Award Level 1 from 1 July 2026 ($26.55 in 2025-26, +4.75% in the Fair Work Commission's Annual Wage Review 2026: $27.81 an hour, 76 hours a fortnight); full-time retail staff are paid close to it (the industry's all-employee median, $900 a week, is mostly part-time). Factory and construction: the industries' median weekly earnings in main job, $1,500 each (ABS, Employee Earnings, August 2025; all employees, mostly full-time in these industries), two weeks.
sources.rents_per_month: Weekly rents x 52/12. Regional Victoria medians: $470 a week overall (Homes Victoria, Rental Report, September quarter 2025); houses $495-530, units $400 (REIV, early 2026). The split by bedrooms ($340, $410, $470 for units of 1-3 bedrooms; $490 and $570 for houses of 3 and 4) is a placeholder around those medians, to replace with the Rental Report's tables by bedrooms. The apartment mix and house shares are placeholders.
sources.spending.saving_bps: The household saving ratio, 6.5% (ABS, Australian National Accounts: National Income, Expenditure and Product, June quarter 2026).
sources.spending.wealth_effect_bps_per_year: About 3 cents of consumption a year per dollar of wealth (Dvornak & Kohler 2003, 'Housing wealth, stock market wealth and consumption: a panel analysis for Australia', RBA RDP 2003-07; to confirm the figure used).
sources.spending.shops_known: How many sellers a household deals with and knows the prices of: 7 (Lengnick, M. (2013), 'Agent-based macroeconomics: A baseline model', Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization 86, Table 1: n = 7 type A connections; read 2026-10-08). Not a figure of this place: a model's, kept until a survey of shops used is found (the nearest found: 4.4 grocery stores a month for a household in the United States, an industry figure reported in the press; to confirm).
sources.spending.shop_search_bps_per_month: The monthly chance that a household looks at the price of a seller it does not deal with: 25% (Lengnick 2013, Table 1: the probability of searching for a cheaper seller, 0.25 a month; read 2026-10-08). A model's figure, as above.
sources.spending.essentials_per_month: Placeholder: what a person spends however little comes in.
sources.retirement_age: The Age Pension age, 67 (Services Australia). Since 2026-10-08 people here stop work at ages of their own, drawn from labour_force_share_by_age; this age is still the one the profile's other figures turn on (the retired's savings, the end of the payments for those out of work, a retirement fund's access) and the top of the working ages the measures use. The pension's age is the payment's own (support.payments).
sources.savings_by_age: An adult's cash and deposits (not superannuation, not property), by age: the 10th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 90th percentiles; drawn between them, and above the 90th up to three times it. Placeholders shaped by the ABS Survey of Income and Housing (household wealth: deposits by age of reference person), per adult; to confirm against the SIH tables.
sources.retiree_savings: Placeholder: savings at retirement, $150,000-350,000, around typical superannuation balances at 65-69 (to confirm against ATO or ASFA figures).
sources.support.payments: [The pension:] Age Pension, single, maximum rate with supplements: $1,200.90 a fortnight from 20 March 2026 (Department of Social Services, rates from 20 March 2026). Couples' rates and means tests left out. [The payment to those out of work:] JobSeeker Payment, single, no children: $808.70 a fortnight from 20 March 2026 (Department of Social Services). From age 22 (younger people are on Youth Allowance, left out). Means test left out. SHAPE (2026-10-08, track D of docs/design/profile-depth.md): support is now a list of payments, each a rule in three parts: who qualifies, how much, for how long (docs/behaviour/boundary.md); the law is published and the payments office reads it. The payments for those out of work end the year before the profile's retirement age (to_age): the rule the generator applied to every profile until now, written into the payment, where it can be changed. Two payments, the same figures: nothing is changed. Both are flat, with no time limit and no means test, as before: the Age Pension's income and assets tests and the JobSeeker income test could now be said in part (`who.income_under`: a household's income as the claimant declares it), but this note gives no figures for them.
sources.firm_ownership.forms_bps: How the firms of each kind are held (docs/behaviour/firm-ownership.md). Shops and landlords are small businesses, held closely: 97.4% of Australian businesses have fewer than 20 employees, and of those that employ anyone 92.6% do (ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, July 2022 to June 2026, released 18 August 2026); about two-thirds of businesses are family businesses (KPMG and Family Business Australia surveys, 67%; to confirm); rented homes are owned by individual investors, about 70% of them with one property (RBA Bulletin, May 2026, Insights from New Data on Australian Housing Investors). Placeholders, to source: the share of shops (20%) and of landlords (30%) owned from outside the town (a chain's branch; an investor living elsewhere), carried over from the figure this replaces; factories all widely held (a works of 40 is a medium business: 2.4% of businesses have 20 to 199 employees; how many regional ones are family companies, to source).
sources.firm_ownership.closely_held: households_bps: a placeholder (one owning household 85%, two 12%, three 3%), shaped by partnerships being 7.0% of businesses and sole proprietors 30.1% (ABS, Counts of Australian Businesses, June 2026); the number of households behind a company or trust, to source. owner_wealth_fifth_bps: households in the highest fifth of wealth held 85% of the value of business assets (RBA Bulletin, April 2009, The Composition and Distribution of Household Wealth in Australia, from HILDA 2006); the split of the other 15% among the lower fifths is a placeholder.
sources.firm_ownership.widely_held: outside_bps: a placeholder carried over from the figure this replaces (a factory is mostly owned by companies and investors elsewhere), to source. The town's part is held by the households that hold shares directly (a world that turns the retirement fund on gives the fund its share of it: retirement_fund).
sources.firm_ownership.direct_holders: by_wealth_fifth_bps: households holding shares directly, by fifth of wealth: 8% of the lowest, 25% of the second, 72% of the highest, 38% of all (RBA Bulletin, April 2009, from HILDA 2006; 34% of all in 2010, RBA Bulletin, March 2012; 38% of adults held listed investments in 2023, ASX Australian Investor Study 2023); the third and fourth fifths (35%, 50%) are placeholders chosen so that the five average 38%. firms_held: a placeholder (one to four companies each), to source.
sources.retirement_fund: Figures for a retirement fund, used only by a world that asks for one (retirement_fund: true in its description; off unless asked for: docs/behaviour/firm-ownership.md). share_bps_of_local: of the town's part of a widely held firm, the fund's share: households' superannuation reserves were 4,433.1 billion dollars and their shares and other equity 1,749.5 billion at June 2026, 72% and 28% of the two together (ABS, Australian National Accounts: Finance and Wealth, June quarter 2026); a liberty: not all of superannuation is in shares, and households' equity includes unlisted businesses. member_bps: 84% of households held superannuation in 2014 (RBA Bulletin, June 2016, Household Wealth in Australia: Evidence from the 2014 HILDA Survey); of households, used here of adults (to confirm per person). pension_every_days: an account-based pension is paid monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly, as the member chooses (Moneysmart, Account-based pensions); monthly here. drawdown_bps_by_age: the least a pension must pay of the balance a year: 4% under 65, 5% at 65 to 74, 6% at 75 to 79, 7% at 80 to 84, 9% at 85 to 89, 11% at 90 to 94, 14% from 95 (Moneysmart, Account-based pensions). cost_bps_of_income: derived: fees of about 1.1% of assets a year (Productivity Commission, Superannuation: Assessing Efficiency and Competitiveness, 2018; to confirm) over a yearly return of 7.4% (APRA, Quarterly superannuation statistics, March 2026) is about 15% of what a fund's holdings earn.
sources.industry: Placeholders to confirm: manufacturing's compensation of employees and intermediate inputs as shares of output (about 20% and 67%, ABS, Australian National Accounts: Input-Output Tables); retail trade's purchases of goods and wages as shares of sales (about 70% and 14%, ABS, Australian Industry).
sources.prices: Placeholders: an item of goods worth $100 at world prices (the unit the town counts in); imports 10% dearer (freight and margins); inputs $2.50 a kg; building materials $1.25 a kg (docs/behaviour/building.md).
sources.elections.compulsory_voting: Added 2026-10-08 by the platform change that made this a profile figure; needs its author's check. Voting in council elections is compulsory for enrolled residents (Local Government Act 2020 (Vic), s 266; see elections).
sources.ordinary_hours_per_week: Maximum ordinary hours for a full-time employee, 38 a week (Fair Work Act 2009, s 62, the National Employment Standards).
sources.fertility_per_10000: ABS, Births, Australia 2024: births per 10,000 women (the published rates per 1,000, times 10: configs are integers) a year, by age.
sources.labour_force_participation_bps: Placeholder: the share of working-age adults (18 to the retirement age) in the labour force, about 80%; to confirm against ABS, Labour Force, Australia, Table 16 (15-64 year olds). Those outside it (studying, caring, other reasons) don't look for work.
sources.labour_force_share_by_age: ILOSTAT, 'Labour force participation rate by sex and age (%)', five-year bands (dataflow DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT, https://sdmx.ilo.org/rest/data/ILO,DF_EAP_DWAP_SEX_AGE_RT/all?startPeriod=2019; the data file opened and these figures read from it, 2026-10-08), persons, Australia, national, annual 2025, from the ABS Labour Force Survey: ages 25 to 54, 87.003%; 55 to 59, 77.523%; 60 to 64, 61.001%; 65 and over, 16.129%. National, not regional Victoria (no table by age for the region was found); not checked against the ABS (Labour Force, Australia, Detailed)'s own table (to confirm). How it is used: the first band is the reference; someone in the labour force stops work at the start of a later band with the chance these shares give, and those still in at the last band never stop. The survey's last band is open (65 and over), so nobody is drawn to stop after 65, and those who work on are older on average than they are in fact: to split when the shares at 65 to 69, 70 to 74 and 75 and over are opened. The profile's own participation figure (labour_force_participation_bps) still says how many are in the labour force at the reference ages; this curve says only how that share falls with age.
sources.tenancy: Residential Tenancies Act 1997 (Vic), s 44: a residential rent may be increased no more than once every 12 months, with at least 60 days' written notice. After a fixed term, a tenancy continues as a periodic (month-to-month) one unless it's ended by notice or a new agreement (the Act; Consumer Affairs Victoria's guidance on fixed-term agreements, to confirm the section).
sources.values: Placeholder: Schwartz's ten basic values, in the pan-cultural order of importance Schwartz and Bardi found across 56 nations (benevolence, universalism, self-direction, security, conformity, hedonism, achievement, tradition, stimulation, power: 'Value hierarchies across cultures', Journal of Cross-Cultural Psychology 32(3), 2001; to confirm), as importance from 7,000 down to 3,400 basis points, each with a spread of 1,500. To source for this place: the World Values Survey's Schwartz items for Australia (wave 6), rescaled.
sources.industrial_action: Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth), Part 3-3: a protected action ballot needs at least 50% of the members on the roll voting (s 459(1)(b)) and more than 50% of the votes approving (s 459(1)(c)); at least 3 working days' written notice of action (s 414(2)(a), taken as 3 days); an employer must not pay employees for a period of protected action (s 470).
sources.world_price_process: Placeholder: world prices move each month by a mean-reverting random process (sd of the monthly move, in basis points of the base price; the share of a gap from the base kept each month). To estimate from ABS, International Trade Price Indexes (import and export price indexes by commodity).
sources.credit.cash_rate_bps: The RBA's cash rate target, 4.35% (held on 11 August 2026).
sources.credit.funding_spread_bps: Placeholder: what a small bank pays over the cash rate for its funding.
sources.credit.lending_rate_bps: Organisations: small-business loans' average outstanding rate, 7.39% (RBA, May 2026). People: placeholder, to confirm against RBA indicator lending rates for personal loans (Table F5).
sources.credit.serviceability_buffer_bps: APRA's serviceability buffer: lenders assess borrowers at least 3 percentage points above the loan's rate (maintained, May 2026).
sources.credit.max_repayment_share_bps: Placeholders: the most of a borrower's monthly income a lender lets repayments take (people 30%, a common lending guide; organisations 20% of what comes in).
sources.credit.arrears_days: Placeholder: a month behind is arrears (a lender's first notice).
sources.credit.default_days: Non-performing at 90 days past due (APRA, Prudential Standard APS 220 Credit Risk Management).
sources.credit.max_months: Placeholder: the longest term for these loans (five years).
sources.credit.reserve: Placeholder: the cash the bank's lending office keeps back and doesn't lend, $100,000. To source.
sources.opening: Placeholders, to source: what each organisation holds on the first day (the bank's own funds $500,000; the town $2,000,000; the builder $300,000; each landlord $600,000; a shop $30,000 where its working capital isn't worked out from its stock and wages; a factory $400,000), and the least an adult in the labour force has saved ($1,000).
sources.town_finance.parks_per_year: Placeholder: the town's yearly parks line, $150,000 (a park a year at about what the builder charges).
sources.town_finance.payment_approval_over: Placeholder: the town's payments procedure needs the mayor's written approval for any payment over $50,000 (a council's financial delegation; to source).
sources.public_finance.income_tax: ATO, individual income tax rates for residents, 2025-26: nil to $18,200; 16% to $45,000; 30% to $135,000; 37% to $190,000; 45% above. The Medicare levy, 2% (ATO), from the singles low-income threshold, $27,222 for 2024-25 (to confirm for 2025-26; the phase-in above it is left out). Employers withhold on each pay reckoned as a year's income (the ATO's tax tables round to dollars, so differ slightly). SHAPE (2026-10-08, track E of docs/design/profile-depth.md): the law is now a list of charges, each with what it is charged on, its schedule, its reliefs and whom it is paid to (docs/behaviour/public-finance.md). Two charges, the same figures: the resident rates on a year's pay, and the levy on the whole of a pay from its threshold. Nothing is changed; both are paid to the general government.
sources.public_finance.grants_per_resident_per_y: Derived: Victoria's 2025-26 general purpose financial assistance grants, $612.0M (Victorian Local Government Grants Commission, 2025-26 annual allocation report, tabled September 2025), over Victoria's population, about 6.98 million (ABS, National, state and territory population, 2025; to confirm). Local roads grants ($218.3M) are left out: the town has no roads yet.
sources.public_finance.rates_per_resident_per_ye: Derived: Victorian councils' rates and charges, 51% of $15.3B revenue in 2024-25 (VAGO, Results of 2024-25 Audits: Local Government), over about 6.9 million residents: about $1,131 a resident a year (to confirm). Sets the town's opening rate in the dollar.
sources.public_finance.rates_instalments: Local Government Act 1989 (Vic), s 167: rates are payable in four instalments (or as a lump sum).
sources.public_finance.rates_due_days: Placeholder: an instalment falls due 30 days after its notice.
sources.public_finance.rates_penalty_interest_bp: Local Government Act 1989 (Vic), s 172: interest on unpaid rates at the rate fixed under the Penalty Interest Rates Act 1983, 10% a year (to confirm the current rate).
sources.public_finance.rates_exempt_kinds: Land used exclusively for charitable, educational or public health purposes is not rateable (Local Government Act 1989 (Vic), s 154; to confirm): here, the clinic's, the school's, the police station's (Crown land) and the utilities' (land used for water supply is exempt; the energy retailer's substation is treated alike, a liberty).
sources.public_finance.median_house_price: Valuer-General Victoria, A Guide to Property Values 2024 (released July 2025): country Victoria's median house price, $572,000. The land value of a lot is derived from it: this less what the builder charges to build a house.
sources.services.waste_per_person_per_day_g: Derived: 512 kg of municipal solid waste per person a year, 2022-23 (DCCEEW, National Waste and Resource Recovery Report 2024), a day's worth in grams.
sources.services.landfill_levy_per_tonne: EPA Victoria, waste levy 2025-26: municipal waste in rural areas, $84.78 a tonne. What the landfill charges on top (its gate fee) is left out.
sources.services.council_staff_per_1000: Derived: about 40,600 FTE in Victorian councils at 30 June 2023 (Vic Councils, Local government facts) over about 6.9 million residents: about 6 per 1,000 (to confirm against the MAV workforce report). In the town, all of them are its works crew.
sources.services.collect_seconds_per_10kg: Placeholder: a one-driver side-loader lifts up to 6 bins a minute (Bucher Municipal, Sport side loader); with driving between houses, about 1,000 bins a day is taken as a round, and a household's week of waste as about 24 kg: about 12 seconds of work per 10 kg.
sources.services.asset_life_years: Placeholder: a park or civic building wears out in 15 years without upkeep (after VAGO, Maintaining Local Roads: spray seals last 10-15 years).
sources.services.upkeep_hours_per_week_per_asset: Placeholder: a crew member's half a day a week keeps a park or the hall up (mowing, bins, repairs).
sources.services.complain_bps: Placeholder: the chance a week that a household whose waste has gone two weeks uncollected writes to the town. Who reports and who doesn't varies (the service-request literature, e.g. Stowers 2022, State and Local Government Review); a rate is to be sourced.
sources.unions.membership_bps: ABS, Trade union membership, August 2024: 13.1% of employees; by industry, manufacturing 9.0%, construction 11.7%, retail trade 7.0%, public administration and safety 23.1% (the industry figures to confirm against the release's tables); `other`, the overall rate. Keyed by the industries employers' postings name.
sources.unions.resignation_notice_days: Fair Work (Registered Organisations) Act 2009 (Cth), s 174: a member may resign by written notice, which takes effect two weeks after it's received (or at once, if the member is no longer eligible; to confirm against the section). Written into each membership as the member's notice.
sources.groups.leave_notice_days: Placeholder: a member may leave a club or congregation at once (a voluntary association; a club's own rules may ask for notice). Written into each membership as the member's notice.
sources.unions.dues_per_month: Placeholder: about $14 a week, around what large Australian unions charge full-time members (to source).
sources.unions.claim_margin_bps: Placeholder: a union claims the year's rise in prices and 2% more. Settlements are measured against the Department of Employment and Workplace Relations' Trends in Federal Enterprise Bargaining (average annualised wage increases in new agreements), a calibration target.
sources.households.age_bands_bps: ABS, Census 2021 QuickStats, Rest of Vic. (GCCSA 2RVIC): people by five-year age group (median age 43); 85 and over taken to 99. The ages of adults living alone, as couples without children at home, or in groups are drawn from this, less the parents the family shares imply (the generator derives it: docs/behaviour/households.md).
sources.unions.meeting_every_days: Placeholder: a members' meeting a month.
sources.groups.kinds: The kinds of social group the ABS General Social Survey counts (sport or physical recreation; religious or spiritual; arts or heritage; craft or practical hobby; other recreational or special interest: the category list to confirm against the survey's glossary). How often each meets, and for how long, are placeholders. Whether people come is theirs: the survey's participation is a calibration target (targets), not a rate given to anyone.
sources.groups.taking_part_bps: Calibrated (2026-09-30): the share of adults who belong to a group at the start (which kind: evenly, a placeholder) and go to its gatherings; after that, whether anyone goes is theirs. The survey counts anyone who took part over 12 months (ABS, General Social Survey 2019: 50.0% of people aged 18 and over), which is more than belong at any one time, so it is the target (targets), not this share. At 50% here, a year's participation came out at 60%.
sources.groups.kinds.teaching: What a group asks people to hold, in its words: content, for belief to attach to (docs/design/ai-citizens.md 5). The congregation's stands for the Christian denominations together (one congregation per town is a simplification).
sources.groups.kinds.held_at_start_bps: ABS, Census of Population and Housing 2021: 43.9% of people reported a Christian affiliation (to confirm against the release; other religions, 10.0%, aren't represented yet). At the start, the congregation's members hold its teaching strongly, and others up to this share hold it less; after that it strengthens, spreads and fades.
sources.unions.teaching: The union movement's claim, in words (content for belief). Its members hold it at the start.
sources.groups.per_kind_per_1000_people: Placeholder: one group of each kind for every 1,000 people.
sources.households.child_max_age: The census counts children of any age living with their parents; the ABS family coding counts full-time students to 24 as dependent children. Children at home are drawn up to 24 (a simplification: older children at home are left out).
